results.content: After coil embolization, recanalization through a previously treated feeder is the predominant persistence pattern, reported to exceed 90%.7 Factors such as coil pack­ ing density, the use of oversized coils, and the distance between the coil and the ve­ nous sac have been identified as substan­ tial factors affecting persistence rates.6,31,32 In a recent study by Shimohira et al.13, the location of embolization relative to the last normal branch of the pulmonary artery was determined to be a substantial factor in per­ sistence, as assessed by CT, time-resolved MR angiography, and DSA.
